$comment: Single source of truth for presets. Read by TypeScript (src/presets) and by
Python (tools/generate_precomputed.py), so a preset cannot be defined in the
app in a form Python never validated.
THE TWO MATCHED DATE PAIRS ARE THE TWO ENDS OF THE FLOOD.
1. The Flood BEGINS at the Precambrian-Cambrian boundary. This is the
pre-Flood/Flood contact and a fixed assumption of the model, not a
variable -- see `flood_start_boundary` below.
2. The Flood ENDS at the boundary the reader selects: Cretaceous-Paleogene
or Neogene-Quaternary. This is the Flood/post-Flood contact and it is
the variable input -- see `terminal_boundaries`.
The ACCELERATION is instantaneous -- lambda spikes at t_F and decays as a
single exponential, so t_F == t_F2. What lasts a year is the Flood's
DEPOSITION: `flood_duration_years` gives how long after the onset the
Flood/post-Flood contact was laid down, and that later instant is the
second pair's true age. Because lambda is still falling across that year,
each unit deposited during it records a different acceleration, which is
why the ratios keep climbing into the deep past rather than plateauing.
Everything between those two boundaries is Flood deposition, laid down in a
single year under an enormously accelerated decay rate. Everything above the
terminal boundary is post-Flood, and carries essentially no acceleration.
Naming rule: a value ending in _age is an AGE (years before present), one
ending in _date is a DATE (years after Day 1 of Creation).
PROVISIONAL: the septuagint chronology values are placeholders chosen to
exercise a longer timeline. They are on the pre-publication checklist in
frontend_plan.md and must be reviewed, with a citation, before this ships.

flood_start_boundary.note: Pre-Flood/Flood contact. Fixed: the acceleration onset.

$flood_duration_note: Depositional span, not the acceleration window. Sets the second pair's true age at flood_start_date + this.

flood_only.label: Flood only
note: No Creation-week acceleration, and an instantaneous acceleration onset
(t_F == t_F2) relaxing as a single exponential. The Flood's one-year
depositional span is a constraint age, not a model interval.

general.label: Creation week + Flood
note: Authored but not exposed in v1. Turning this on is flipping `enabled`;
no component changes, because the parameter panel iterates the free
names Python returns rather than a hardcoded list.
Freeing lambda_c/k_c does not disturb the calibration: both constraint
ages map to formation DATEs at or after t_F, so their integrals cover
only the Flood and post-Flood regions and the Creation-week parameters
never enter. Verified to exactly zero difference.
